name: Paper Cutout Illustration
visualIdentity: Objects are built from clearly cut paper shapes with thin visible edges and soft contact shadows. Keep materials and paper colors limited, with consistent shading and one light direction.
suitableUses: Fits illustrated stories, mascots, product explainers, and calm narrative scenes. It can also support interactive HTML with bounded pointer or scroll responses. These are inferred uses from the style and compatible motion patterns.
limitations: Avoid intersecting pieces, conflicting shadows, excessive materials, or motion that breaks joints and contact. Use parallax only with enough layered artwork and crop margin; quantified diagrams need geometry that preserves the data. Keep labels readable and motion accessible.
palette: Optional four-token proposal: background cream #F2EAD8, foreground ink #304849, terracotta #C17F63, and sage #829776. Supplied or approved colors and role assignments take priority; preserve color families and asset colors. Use discrete tokens, no added gradients. Terracotta and sage are decorative only for body text; recheck contrast on final composites.
motionAndInteraction: Animate pieces around believable joints with sliding, rotation, and folding. Define pivots and parent-child connections; avoid intersections and conflicting shadows. For video, derive states from seekable composition time. HTML may add bounded pointer or scroll interaction, with keyboard and reduced-motion support where applicable. Parallax, gaze, and chapter patterns are optional and require suitable assets and scene rationale.
audio: Unspecified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio requirements. Synchronize and mix with picture, keep speech clear, and check clipping and sync.
assetRequirements: Prepare paper contours, transparent layered artwork or numbered frames, and contact shadows; inspect dimensions, naming, and transparency. Define pivots and connections for movable pieces. Paper.js can prepare 2D paths; SVG or PixiJS can render layers. Three.js is optional only when actual depth or curling is needed; flat scenes can use SVG or Canvas.
combinations: Paper Cutout alone suits stories told by jointed pieces. Optional restrained parallax adds depth to stacked planes while preserving one light direction and moving pieces only at their joints. Paper-cut diagrams can show verified comparisons if geometry encodes data accurately, with cosmetic edge irregularity. These hybrids are suggestions, not requirements.
productionApproach: Select the visual renderer and motion engine for the art and action; each animated property needs one owner. Use deterministic, seekable state or baked assets. HyperFrames is the primary video assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; Remotion is only a documented fallback. For HTML, use native SVG/DOM or suitable renderers with bounded input behavior. Validate representative states and composites; audio and final export are pipeline responsibilities.
